leads.claim: MadHatter cipher (Jan 2020; its ciphertext was a bonus challenge in the 2019 British National Cipher Challenge): ciphertext alphabet A-I, plaintext is 24 letters (J->I, Z->S), each letter becomes a 4-symbol block with one symbol from each of {A,B},{C,D},{E,F},{G,H,I} (mixed radix 2,2,2,3). The block is then permuted by a second plaintext letter (24 permutations of 4) -> two plaintexts in one ciphertext. This fits the a-i alphabet of SalPhaseIon dbbi/faed and the 'Cosmic Duality'/yin-yang/'half and better half' theme. Hand check this cycle: the dbbi stream as quoted in the solving doc has adjacent repeats (b b at 2-3, c c at 9-10, g g at 26-27, b b at 33-34, h h at 37-38). Their positions mod 4 are 2,1,2,1,1, so no 4-block alignment avoids a repeated symbol inside a block, and dbbi is NOT MadHatter-structured. faed was not checked here.
leads.method: structural test: for each alignment, split into 4-blocks and require 4 distinct symbols with exactly one from each group (search all 2,2,2,3 partitions of a-i); if structured, decode block->(mixed-radix letter, permutation letter) under keyed alphabets
leads.self_verifying: a random a-i stream almost never has every 4-block contain one symbol from each of 4 fixed groups; if faed (or any segment) passes, the structure itself is the proof. Without that, the test is negative in seconds.

leads.claim: Cosmic Duality candidate (solver claim from GitHub issue #55, 2025-08-23): XOR of SHA-256 digests of the 7 SalPhaseIon tokens is used as an OpenSSL MD5-EVP AES-256-CBC password. It gives a 1,327-byte high-entropy plaintext. A matrixsumlist reading of it (103x103 bits, row[i]+col[(i+7) mod 103], base 38 with digit ord-80) gives 68 bytes = Half and Better Half keys + trailer fc0c1b02. Then come the Chain4 1,151-byte output and the 31+35x32 geometry. The baseline itself demotes all of this: only a ~1/256 padding signal, and the hash is self-referential.
leads.method: openssl EVP_BytesToKey(MD5) AES-256-CBC with raw 32-byte XOR password; matrix row/col sums; repeating-XOR Salted__ header recovery
leads.self_verifying: No. Padding-only acceptance (~1/256 false-positive rate) with high-entropy output. The component keys give empty addresses, not the prize. Chain4 needs the unauthenticated Cosmic key.

leads.claim: Deduplicating dbbi by first occurrence gives keyword dbifhcega. Keyed Bifid over all of faed (one full-period block) gives the 'btcseed' header plus a 563-char remainder (563 is the 103rd prime). That remainder is split as 281 + central d + 281, and a unique z switches pair orientation, giving 281 symbols over 4x24 = 96 states. 8 of the 9! a-i keyword orders reproduce the btcseed prefix (1 in 45,360).
leads.self_verifying: the 7-letter header is reproducible; the remainder is not readable

leads.claim: Standard walkthrough decodes: SalPhaseIon abba bits -> matrixsumlist, enter. a-i/o digits (o=0) -> decimal -> hex -> ASCII gives lastwordsbeforearchichoice and thispassword. shabef = sha256 under a1z26. Stage passwords are hashed with sha256 and used as openssl -pass. The SalPhaseIon AES blob and an extra blob are left as '<TO GUESS>'.

Points 2P..5P and halving P/2, P/4, P/8 of the prize pubkey, with their addresses (e.g. -Y P2PKH 1LzLrZVkafbXLpam3qibRDdMe5sttUoCq4; compressed +Y 1cc6xayvqpeetixmuXDRsGug7GKyoRdxP). No private key is involved; this is just point arithmetic on a known public key and cannot reveal the scalar.
leads.self_verifying: the arithmetic verifies, but it carries no information about the key
